intent: session cleanup Phase 2B: extract audit decision-source branches into separable functions
notes: Phase 2B of the [2026-08-11 non-Enterprise session cleanup plan](vault/artifacts/2026-08-11-non-enterprise-session-cleanup-plan.md) — the second deletion-free reshape. Refactors `gator-audit.py::assemble_audit_data()` so the two `decisions_source` branches live in cleanly-separable module-level functions, making Phase 3's deletion mechanical.

Extracted `_committed_decisions_from_snippets(reader_mod, sessions_dirs_tagged, has_remote_sessions, data, since_days)` — the snippet-reader branch (previously ~60 inline lines inside the `if has_committed or has_remote_sessions:` block). **SURVIVING** contract per parent plan §2.1. Returns `(committed_decisions, summary_items)`. Behavior byte-identical to the pre-extraction inline body.

Extracted `_committed_decisions_from_raw_vendor_logs(sessions_mod, common, since_days, data)` — the raw-vendor-logs branch (previously ~55 inline lines inside the `elif common:` block). **DELETE-VENDOR** — retires in Phase 3 with the vendor-transcript archaeology. Docstring notes the Phase 3 mechanical deletion recipe (delete function + delete `elif common:` dispatch site). Behavior byte-identical.

`assemble_audit_data()`'s decision-source dispatch is now a 14-line `if/elif` (was ~115 inline lines): each branch sets `data["decisions_source"]` + `data["decisions_dirs"]` + optional `data["session_summaries"]`, then calls its helper. The outer `if sessions_mod:` guard is preserved (behavior-neutral) — Phase 3 removes the outer guard when the vendor branch retires.

Both helpers preserve the original data-mutation contract: snippets helper pops `data["_remote_sessions"]` if present; vendor helper appends to `data["_errors"]` on outer exceptions. Same call-graph, same exception handling, same return values.

Charter update: `.gator/charters/scripts-fleet-intelligence.md` — `assemble_audit_data()` `->` line extends to mention the two new helpers; new `### _committed_decisions_from_snippets(...)` and `### _committed_decisions_from_raw_vendor_logs(...)` entries with SURVIVING / DELETE-VENDOR tags and full call-in/call-out lists. Phase 3 charter sweep will delete the raw-vendor-logs entry when the code retires.

Verification: `tests/test_audit_integration.py` (3 tests) + `tests/test_session_reader.py` (5 tests) + `tests/test_sessions.py` (45 tests) all PASS. Full test suite: 867 passed, 2 xfailed (pre-existing v2.6.0 xfails). Zero regressions.

Significance-check assessment (constitution step 7): touches no public CLI verb, no cross-module TRIPWIRE (row_key formula + vendor-extractor delegation contract both untouched), no security-relevant code. This is a pure structural reshape of `assemble_audit_data()` — same inputs, same outputs, same side effects. Steelman argument against: extracting a helper that will be deleted in one commit later (Phase 3) may look wasteful. Response: the extraction IS the Phase 3 preparation — it converts a ~55-line diff scattered inside a nested branch into a mechanical whole-function delete + one call-site delete. That mechanical shape is exactly what deletion-free Phase 2 exists to produce.
